newsitem.title: UK: UK insurance system opened to overseas brokers.
newsitem.headline: UK insurance system opened to overseas brokers.

text.p: Insurance brokers around the world, with the exception of North America, will from now on be able to use the London Processing Centre (LPC) computer systems, LIRMA said in a statement.

"Extending use of the LPC to brokers outside Europe is a natural development given the international nature of LIRMA and the growing effectiveness of information technology," LIRMA chairman Philip Marcell said.
The LPC is a computerised bureau which processes insurance premiums and claims worth nearly 10 billion stg a year.
The Centre is owned jointly by industry associations London International Insurance and Reinsurance Market Association (LIRMA) and the Institute of London Underwriters (ILU).
In February last year, the LPC was opened up to European insurers not licensed in the UK.

The latest development will be of particular interest to brokers in the Far East, Australia and New Zealand, a spokesman for LIRMA told Reuters, adding that some had already enquired about processing business through London.
"We're not expecting an avalanche of new business -- expansion will be a long, slow process, but we have the capacity to handle twice the current volume with very few changes," the spokesman said.
Brokers in North America have been excluded for several reasons, including the regulatory regimes in those countries, LIRMA said.
LIRMA and the ILU represent international insurance and reinsurance companies transacting large-scale business through the London Market.
